extracted.intended_audience: improvisers and improv teachers (students at Magnet Theater and other scene-based improv performers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for creating short improvised scenes using a relationship-first approach (including use of forms such as the Armando). Focus is on establishing truthful relationships, honest reactions, discovery, and using form to anchor scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the relationship established within the first three lines?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the relationship established within the first three lines?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magnet house philosophy: Begin EVERY scene by establishing a relationship (lovers, siblings, coworkers, longtime friends). The relationship is the engine; the game is the fuel. Without relationship, comedy is mechanical. The audience invests in PEOPLE more than in patterns and stakes require relationship — establish who the characters are to create investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are characters reacting honestly to offers?
rubrics_metrics.description: Are characters reacting honestly to offers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honest-Reaction Rule: React the way your character honestly would. Honest reactions to absurd offers create the comedy; performative or staged reactions create distance. Evaluate whether each offer in the scene receives an in-character, believable response rather than a performative set-up for a gag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the comedy emerging from the relationship's stress, not random escalation?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the comedy emerging from the relationship's stress, not random escalation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer comedy that grows naturally from tensions, stakes, and dynamics within the established relationship rather than from arbitrary one-upmanship or non sequitur escalation. The game should be fuelled by the relationship, so pay attention to how stress, conflict, and emotional truth produce laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have you DISCOVERED rather than declared the relationship?
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you DISCOVERED rather than declared the relationship?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On Discovery vs. Initiation: The first lines of a scene should discover the relationship as story rather than simply announce it. Anti-pattern: 'Mom, you forgot my birthday' (a declaration that hands the audience data). Pattern: 'Mom, do you remember when you...?' (begins to reveal shared history and dynamics). Discovery creates curiosity and layers; declaration flattens the scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: If using a form, is the form anchoring or constraining?
rubrics_metrics.description: If using a form, is the form anchoring or constraining?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On Form (the Armando): A useful form (like the Armando) starts with a true monologue from a guest monologist; scenes are improvised inspired by that monologue and each scene returns thematically to the monologue's truth. Assess whether the form is helping performers stay anchored in real human experience (anchoring) or forcing them into artificial patterning (constraining).

rubrics_metrics.name: Could the scene make sense even if you removed the punchlines?
rubrics_metrics.description: Could the scene make sense even if you removed the punchlines?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the scene's underlying human truth and coherence: a strong scene should retain emotional logic and story if surface jokes are removed. If the scene only exists to serve punchlines, it likely lacks depth and relationship-based stakes.
